sentences.zh: 我叫杰米·费舍尔，我是《纽约时报》

sentences.zh: 杂志的研究编辑，同时我也是一名自由撰稿人。

sentences.en: My latest piece is about the film and television composer, Nicholas Bertel.
sentences.zh: 我的最新文章是关于电影和电视作曲家尼古拉斯·贝尔特el的。

sentences.en: I don't have a single memory of the first time I heard his music.
sentences.zh: 我完全记不清第一次听到他的音乐是什么时候了。

sentences.en: I just gradually realized that all of the film and television music I was drawn to,
sentences.zh: 我只是渐渐发现，所有吸引我的电影和电视音乐，

sentences.en: invariably, when the credit sequence came up, it would be by Nicholas Bertel.
sentences.zh: 无一例外，当演职员表出现时，创作者都是尼古拉斯·贝尔特el。

sentences.en: How could all of these different projects that are also, I mean, the sound is so accessible and wonderful, how could they all come from the same person when they're so varied?
sentences.zh: 这些风格迥异的项目——而且我是说，它们的声音是如此平易近人又美妙——怎么可能全都出自同一个人之手，明明它们差异这么大？

sentences.en: And I wanted to know, who is Nicholas Bertel?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，尼古拉斯·贝尔特el究竟是谁？

sentences.en: How did he score like a comedy epic, like Vice?
sentences.zh: 他是如何为像《副总统》这样宏大的喜剧史诗谱曲的？

sentences.en: But also, if Beale Street could talk, which has this beautiful, jazzy, analog sound.
sentences.zh: 同时还有《如果比尔街能说话》，那部电影有着美妙、爵士风且带点模拟质感的声音。

sentences.en: And I have a memory of like watching Succession and like more than the plot, what kept me going through the first season was just waiting for this theme that he had written.
sentences.zh: 我记得在看《继承之战》时，比起剧情，支撑我看完第一季的动力其实是等待他写的那段主题音乐。

sentences.en: There's just this fresh sound to it where it's classical music, and then there's these heavy
sentences.zh: 它有一种新鲜感，既有古典音乐，又伴随着沉重的

sentences.en: beats, there's a sleigh bell, and there's this pop that almost sounds like a can of LaCroix popping open.
sentences.zh: 节奏、雪橇铃，还有那种听起来几乎像是 LaCroix 气泡水拉环被拉开时的流行音效。

sentences.en: And it just felt like relentlessly contemporary in the most wonderful way.
sentences.zh: 它以最美妙的方式让人感到一种不依不饶的当代气息。

sentences.en: And I just, I had to know more.
sentences.zh: 我就是忍不住想要了解更多。

sentences.en: I spoke early on with a teacher of Nick's when he had first started to try writing film music,
sentences.zh: 我早期曾采访过尼克的一位老师，那是他刚开始尝试创作电影音乐的时候，

sentences.en: who told me he was just amazed by the cheerful way Nick would scrap everything and start over if he was asked to.
sentences.zh: 那位老师告诉我，尼克在被要求时那种高高兴兴地把一切推倒重来的态度让他惊叹不已。

sentences.en: Just completely in a good spirit, without mourning for the work he'd lost, you know?
sentences.zh: 完全是带着好心态，没有为失去的心血感到哀伤，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And he just made me feel like nothing is ever loSt. The energy that you put into that informs the approach that you take later.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得没有什么东西是真正白费的。你投入进去的精力会为你日后的方法论提供养分。

sentences.en: And the final thing that you get, it's not just what you wanted, it's also what the director wanted.
sentences.zh: 最后呈现的东西，不仅是你想要的，也是导演想要的。

sentences.en: So I reached out to Nick, and we met in his studio back in the fall of
sentences.zh: 于是我联系了尼克，我们在2019年
秋天于他的工作室见面了。

sentences.en: At that point, he just started working on the score for the limited series, The Underground Railroad.
sentences.zh: 那时，他才刚刚开始为限定剧《地下铁路》创作配乐。

sentences.en: And since then, that score has been nominated for an Emmy Award.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，那部配乐获得了艾美奖提名。

sentences.zh: 这就是我的故事：站在

sentences.en: First time I understood what it is that the composer
sentences.zh: 我第一次真正理解作曲家

sentences.en: Nicholas Bertel does for a film, understood with my whole body, I was in his studio listening to a mistake he had made and the way he had fixed it.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉斯·贝尔特el为电影所做的事情是什么，是用整个身体去理解，当时我正坐在他的工作室里，听着他犯过的一个错误以及他是如何修正它的。

sentences.en: Earlier, in a cafe off Lincoln Center, I had asked him about the process of making Moonlight, the Oscar-winning coming-of-age story he scored for
sentences.zh: 早些时候，在林肯中心附近的一家咖啡馆里，我曾向他问起创作《月光男孩》的过程，那是他为

sentences.en: Barry Jenkins.
sentences.zh: 巴里·詹金斯配乐并荣获奥斯卡奖的成长故事片。

sentences.en: Bertel told me about a scene early in the film in which the protagonist's mentor teaches him to swim.
sentences.zh: 贝尔特el向我讲述了片中早期的一个场景：主人公的导师教他游泳。

sentences.en: I was looking at the sequence like, oh, Juan and Little swim, Bertel said.
sentences.zh: 贝尔特el说：“我当时看着这个镜头，心想，哦，胡安和小黑在游泳。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美好的时刻。

sentences.en: This will be something special he can carry with him.
sentences.zh: 这将成为他可以随身携带的特殊回忆。”

sentences.en: So Bertel wrote a sweet piece in F major, an orchestral swell with a clarinet singing a variation on Little's theme on top.
sentences.zh: 于是贝尔特el写了一首F大调的温柔曲子，管弦乐澎湃涌动，上面是一支单关琴在歌唱小黑主题的变奏。

sentences.en: He played it for Jenkins.
sentences.zh: 他弹给詹金斯听。

sentences.en: The response was a visceral nope.
sentences.zh: 得到的反馈是一个发自内心的“不行”。

sentences.en: Jenkins urged him to think of the scene as a spiritual baptism.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯敦促他把这个场景当作一次精神上的洗礼来思考。

sentences.en: This wasn't simple optimism or happiness.
sentences.zh: 这并非简单的乐观或快乐。

sentences.en: It was the first day of the rest of
sentences.zh: 这是

sentences.en: Little's life.
sentences.zh: 小黑余生里的第一天。

sentences.en: And I still get moved even just thinking about it, Bertel said, because I immediately knew.
sentences.zh: 贝尔特el说：“每当回想起来，我依然会深受触动，因为我立刻就懂了。”

sentences.en: On the spot, he began improvising something darker, in D minor, with the virtuosic feeling of a cadenza.
sentences.zh: 他当场开始即兴创作一首更黑暗的曲子，D小调，带有华彩乐段般的炫技感。

sentences.en: I was playing it on my keyboard with a kind of fake violence, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我用键盘弹奏它，带有一种近乎假装的暴力感。”

sentences.en: Barry was directing me from the couch.
sentences.zh: “巴里在沙发上指导我。”

sentences.en: And so right there, I just made it in front of him.
sentences.zh: “所以就在那儿，我在他面前当场创作出来了。”

sentences.en: In his studio, Bertel played me the scene.
sentences.zh: 在工作室里，贝尔特el为我播放了这个场景。

sentences.en: First, he queued up his original attempt over footage from an early cut.
sentences.zh: 首先，他在早期剪辑的画面上播放了他最初的尝试。

sentences.en: It was tender, unambiguous movie music that could have scored any rite of passage.
sentences.zh: 那是温柔、毫无歧义的电影音乐，完全可以给任何成年礼配乐。

sentences.en: I pictured a high school football team triumphing against all odds.
sentences.zh: 我想象着一支高中橄榄球队在逆境中取得胜利。

sentences.en: Then he queued up Middle of the World, the music he made with
sentences.zh: 接着，他播放了《世界的中心》（Middle of the World），这是他和

sentences.en: Jenkins.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯共同创作的音乐。

sentences.en: The violin plays jolting waves of arpeggios, wild and exhilarating.
sentences.zh: 小提琴奏出震撼人心的琶音波浪，狂野而令人振奋。

sentences.en: Little vanishes into the ocean,
sentences.zh: 小黑消失在海洋中，

sentences.en: Juan holding him, but somehow not protecting him, only initiating him into a kind of violent abandon.
sentences.zh: 胡安抱着他，但不知为何并没有保护他，只是将他引入了一种充满暴力的纵情之中。

sentences.en: You watch with your heart in your throat.
sentences.zh: 你看着这一幕，心提到了嗓子眼。

sentences.en: It's beautiful, and also, somehow, terrifying.
sentences.zh: 它很美，同时又莫名地让人感到恐惧。

sentences.en: The studio I was listening in, seated in the same spot Jenkins occupied as the music was written,
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时所坐的工作室——位置和音乐创作时詹金斯坐的地方一模一样——

sentences.en: is the size a New York realtor would market as a child's bedroom in an apartment overlooking the
sentences.zh: 其面积大到足以让纽约房地产经纪人在俯瞰

sentences.en: Hudson.
sentences.zh: 哈德逊河的公寓里将其宣传为儿童卧室。

sentences.en: It's dark, the walls covered with gray acoustic foam, and Bertel often works with the lights off.
sentences.zh: 这里很暗，墙上贴着灰色的吸音泡沫，贝尔特el经常关着灯工作。

sentences.en: He shares the apartment with his wife, the cellist Caitlin Sullivan, who is constantly and correctly encouraging me to take walks.
sentences.zh: 他与妻子、大提琴手凯特琳·沙利文合住这套公寓，她总是且正确地鼓励我出去散步。

sentences.en: She also worries that he drinks too much Perrier.
sentences.zh: 她还担心他喝太多巴黎水。

sentences.en: There are bookshelves and vintage movie posters on the walls.
sentences.zh: 墙上有书架和复古电影海报。

sentences.en: Chariots of Fire greets you at the entrance, and a small sofa, the left side of which is Jenkins' territory.
sentences.zh: 《烈火战车》在入口处迎接你，还有一个小沙发，左半边是詹金斯的领地。

sentences.en: A huge monitor is mounted over Bertel's keyboard for projecting rough cuts.
sentences.zh: 贝尔特el的键盘上方安装了一个巨大的显示器，用于投射粗剪画面。

sentences.en: With a movie-sized screen, you make movie-sized music, Bertel has learned.
sentences.zh: 贝尔特el领悟到：“用电影院大小的屏幕，你就能做出电影院大小的音乐。”

sentences.en: There's also a subwoofer the size of a washing machine.
sentences.zh: 这里还有一个洗衣机大小的低音炮。

sentences.en: Bertel's scores include tones so low that they feel less like something audible and more like approaching weather.
sentences.zh: 贝尔特el的配乐包含了一些极低的音调，听起来与其说像是能听见的声音，倒不如说更像是正在逼近的天气。

sentences.en: Last year, in February,
sentences.zh: 去年2月，

sentences.en: Bertel invited me back to the studio to watch him and Jenkins at work.
sentences.zh: 贝尔特el邀请我回到工作室，观看他和詹金斯工作。

sentences.en: The two hadn't previously allowed anyone to sit in on their sessions, day-long confabs that involve near-clinical infusions of
sentences.zh: 此前两人从未允许任何人旁听他们的创作会议——那是一整天的碰头会，伴随着近乎临床剂量的

sentences.en: Shake Shack.
sentences.zh: Shake Shack 汉堡。

sentences.en: They were still early in their work on the Underground Railroad, a ten-part series based on the novel by Colson Whitehead.
sentences.zh: 他们当时还在《地下铁路》创作的初期阶段，这是一部根据科尔森·怀特黑德小说改编的十集剧集。

sentences.en: It is Bertel's first television collaboration with Jenkins, and his compositions for it are less a single score than ten intersecting, fully realized musical universes.
sentences.zh: 这是贝尔特el与詹金斯的首次电视剧合作，他为此创作的配乐与其说是一个单一的配乐，不如说是十个交织在一起、完全成型的音乐宇宙。

sentences.en: The first piece he played me at the session was something the two men made hours before,
sentences.zh: 他在这次会议上放给我的第一段音乐是这两人几小时前创作的，

sentences.en: a dark, inquisitive piano sequence only a few bars long, circling the drain of a few dissonant notes.
sentences.zh: 一段黑暗、好奇心十足的钢琴旋律，只有短短几个小节，在几个不和谐音符的下水道边缘盘旋。

sentences.en: One of the things we keep discovering is, for some reason, pianos, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我们不断发现的事情之一，不知为何，就是钢琴。”

sentences.en: Really specific pianos, like slightly warped.
sentences.zh: “非常具体的钢琴，比如稍微有些变形的钢琴。”

sentences.en: He played another sequence to demonstrate.
sentences.zh: 他弹奏了另一段旋律来作示范。

sentences.en: It's felted, the piano's hammers are padded with extra cloth, so it's really muffled, but it's always like piano works.
sentences.zh: “装了毛毡的，钢琴的琴锤垫了额外的布料，所以声音很闷，但听起来总是像是钢琴在工作。”

sentences.en: Jenkins sauntered in after finishing his burger in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯在厨房吃完汉堡后溜达了进来。

sentences.en: All he had on hand were a few unedited shots, he explained.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，他手头只有几个未编辑的镜头，

sentences.en: But I like to have some kind of picture while we're working.
sentences.zh: “但我们在工作时还是喜欢有一些画面。”

sentences.en: If it works with this picture, it feels like you can tell it's part of the world.
sentences.zh: “如果它与这个画面契合，你就会觉得它属于这个世界的一部分。”

sentences.en: He had been shooting in Georgia since August and flew up to spend the weekend with Bertel before heading back to the set.
sentences.zh: 他自8月以来一直在佐治亚州拍摄，乘飞机赶来和贝尔特el共度周末，然后就要返回片场。

sentences.en: By this point, his voice sounded felted, too.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，他的声音听起来也像是蒙了一层毛毡。

sentences.en: 92 days, 24 to go, he said, rubbing his face.
sentences.zh: 他揉着脸说：“还剩92天，24天倒计时。”

sentences.en: We don't normally work like this until we're done, but yeah, no choice.
sentences.zh: “我们通常不会这样一直工作到完成，但没办法，别无选择。”

sentences.en: In hindsight, this wasn't quite true.
sentences.zh: 事后看来，这并不完全准确。

sentences.en: Only weeks later, the pandemic would shutter production for months, leaving them to finish their work in a sun-drenched quarantine pod in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 仅几周后，大流行就迫使制作停工数月，迫使他们在洛杉矶一个阳光普照的隔离舱里完成了工作。

sentences.en: Still, by the end of the session, Jenkins had slid down until he was sitting on the floor, slumped against the couch with his hoodie tugged over his face.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，到会议结束时，詹金斯已经滑落到坐在地板上，靠着沙发瘫坐着，连帽衫拉起来蒙住了脸。

sentences.en: You can't make a meal of how tired I am when you write this, he warned.
sentences.zh: 他警告说：“你写这个的时候，可别把我有多累当成卖点。”

sentences.en: I was more struck by how comfortable the two men seemed together.
sentences.zh: 更让我印象深刻的是这两个人在一起时显得多么自在。

sentences.en: Bertel's voice even sounded different when he was with Jenkins, half an octave down, words running together easily.
sentences.zh: 跟詹金斯在一起时，贝尔特el连声音听起来都不一样了，降低了半个八度，字句轻松地连在一起。

sentences.en: You have to understand, Jenkins said.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯说：“你得明白。”

sentences.en: When we did Moonlight, I didn't really know Nick at that point.
sentences.zh: “我们做《月光男孩》的时候，那时候我其实并不认识尼克。”

sentences.en: This is the origin of the Jenkins-Bertel partnership, the filmmaking equivalent of buying a house unseen.
sentences.zh: 这就是詹金斯与贝尔特el合作关系的起源，相当于电影制作版本的“盲买房子”。

sentences.en: The producer, Jeremy Kleiner, had arranged an afternoon coffee between the men, which turned into evening drinks, the two of them talking for hours, mostly not about music.
sentences.zh: 制片人杰里米·克莱纳安排两人下午喝咖啡，结果演变成了晚间饮酒，两人聊了好几个小时，大部分时候聊的都不是音乐。

sentences.en: They just vibed the whole time, Sullivan told me, and Barry hired him.
sentences.zh: 沙利文告诉我：“他们全程都极其合拍，然后巴里就雇了他。”

sentences.en: He hired him never having heard any samples of Nick's music of any kind.
sentences.zh: “他雇佣他时，甚至压根没听过尼克的任何音乐小样。”

sentences.en: We had one meeting, Jenkins said.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯说：“我们开了一次会。”

sentences.en: We went off and shot the film, and then it was like, oh, just come to New York.
sentences.zh: “然后我们去拍了电影，接着就变成了，‘哦，直接来纽约吧。’”

sentences.en: And so I walk into this place, he said, giving considerable side-eye to the premises.
sentences.zh: 他斜眼狠狠打量了一下这个地方，说道：“所以我走进了这个地方。”

sentences.en: We're gonna work in your bedroom?
sentences.zh: “我们要在一个卧室里工作？”

sentences.en: How's that gonna work?
sentences.zh: “这怎么行得通？”

sentences.en: But he made all this wonderful music.
sentences.zh: “但他做出了所有这些美妙的音乐。”

sentences.en: So yeah, now it's like a little home away from home.
sentences.zh: “所以，是的，现在这里就像是个温馨的小避风港。”

sentences.zh: 他在2015年的一场车祸中丧生，当时贝尔特尔的音乐事业正处于腾飞阶段。

sentences.en: He was the first person to ask Bertel to write a score, and the question proved transformative.
sentences.zh: 他是第一个请贝尔特尔写配乐的人，而这个问题具有变革性的意义。

sentences.en: We were always working on this movie, and I was always with the band, and those experiences really defined my life, Bertel says.
sentences.zh: “我们当时一直在制作这部电影，我也一直跟乐队在一起，那些经历真正定义了我的人生，”贝尔特尔说。

sentences.en: But the band broke up after college, and the film he'd done with Lavelle wasn't headed to theaters anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 但大学毕业后乐队解散了，他与拉维尔合作的那部电影短期内也不会上映。

sentences.en: A classmate who worked at
sentences.zh: 一位在

sentences.en: Bear Stearns suggested that Bertel consider interviewing.
sentences.zh: 贝尔斯登工作的同学建议贝尔特尔考虑去面试。

sentences.en: He got an offer and took it.
sentences.zh: 他拿到了一份offer并接受了。

sentences.en: I was thinking to myself, oh, in six months I'll probably go, Bertel recalls.
sentences.zh: 贝尔特尔回忆道：“我当时心里想，哦，我大概六个月后就会离开吧。”

sentences.en: Lavelle's film would break out.
sentences.zh: 拉维尔的电影会大获成功。

sentences.en: People would snap up the beats he was ending around.
sentences.zh: 人们会抢购他四处发送的那些节拍。

sentences.en: Someone would hire him to produce.
sentences.zh: 会有人雇他去担任制作人。

sentences.en: Except none of that happened.
sentences.zh: 然而这些都没有发生。

sentences.en: For years.
sentences.zh: 持续了好多年。

sentences.en: Caitlin Sullivan, Bertel's wife, has played on nearly all his scores, including a melody symbolizing love in Beale Street.
sentences.zh: 凯特琳·沙利文（Caitlin Sullivan），贝尔特尔的妻子，几乎参与了他所有的配乐演奏，包括《如果比尔街能说话》中象征爱情的旋律。

sentences.en: She is also the reason Bertel is not researching emerging market currencies in a midtown office.
sentences.zh: 她也是贝尔特尔没有在中城区的一间办公室里研究新兴市场货币的原因。

sentences.en: The two first met when they were 18, studying music at a summer program in Aspen,
sentences.zh: 两人最初相识是在18岁时，当时他们在科罗拉多州阿斯彭的一个暑期项目

sentences.en: Colorado.
sentences.zh: 学习音乐。

sentences.en: This despite years of attending the same Juilliard program.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们多年来一直参加同一个茱莉亚音乐学院的项目。

sentences.en: They reunited after college, when Sullivan was embarking on her career as a professional celliSt. She took Bertel out for a
sentences.zh: 大学毕业后他们重聚了，当时沙利文正开始她作为职业大提琴手的职业生涯。2005年，她带贝尔特尔出去吃

sentences.en: birthday dinner in 2005, and they have been together ever since.
sentences.zh: 生日晚餐，从那以后他们就一直在一起。

sentences.en: By that point, Bertel had been in finance for about a year, traveling to interview central bankers and people in finance ministries in Europe and East Asia.
sentences.zh: 到那时为止，贝尔特尔在金融界已经工作了大约一年，四处奔波去采访欧洲和东亚的中央银行家以及财政部官员。

sentences.en: He thought he was happy.
sentences.zh: 他以为自己很幸福。

sentences.en: If you're a curious person, Sullivan observes, a hyper-competent person, it's sometimes hard to actually parse out your true feelings.
sentences.zh: 沙利文观察到：“如果你是一个好奇心强、能力极高的人，有时其实很难真正剖析出你真实的感受。”

sentences.en: For years, she watched him come home and play the piano or improvise beats on his old keyboard.
sentences.zh: 多年来，她看着他回到家里弹钢琴，或者在旧键盘上即兴创作节拍。

sentences.en: He'd be up, in a suit, gone around 7.30 a.m.
sentences.zh: 她说，他会起床穿好西装，

sentences.en: every day and home around dinner time, she says.
sentences.zh: 每天早上七点半左右出门，晚饭时间左右回家。

sentences.en: But he would need to touch the piano.
sentences.zh: 但他就是需要碰一碰钢琴。

sentences.en: He scrounged time for projects with friends, including short films for a former classmate, Natalie Portman.
sentences.zh: 他千方百计挤出时间与朋友们合作项目，包括为老同学娜塔莉·波特曼拍摄短片。

sentences.en: In one of her films, he made a cameo as a cocktail pianist, tucked discreetly behind Lauren Bacall.
sentences.zh: 在她的其中一部电影中，他客串了一位鸡尾酒会钢琴师，低调地隐身于劳伦·白考尔身后。

sentences.en: In 2008, on a vacation, Sullivan watched the heavy way Bertel would pull out his BlackBerry to check the markets.
sentences.zh: 2008年的一次度假中，沙利文注意到贝尔特尔掏出黑莓手机查看行情时那副沉重疲惫的神情。

sentences.en: For months, he had been so depressed that it felt like vertigo.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，他一直感到极其沮丧，甚至有了眩晕感。

sentences.en: But until Sullivan told him he was unhappy, he hadn't fully known it.
sentences.zh: 但直到沙利文告诉他他并不快乐之前，他自己并没有完全意识到这一点。

sentences.en: The markets, meanwhile, had guttered, Bear Stearns had folded in front of his eyes, and terrifyingly, the smartest people he knew had no idea what was going on.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，市场已经崩盘，贝尔斯登在他眼前倒闭，更可怕的是，他所认识最聪明的人也不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: People were traumatized, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：“人们都受到了创伤。”

sentences.en: It was scary to see that end to what I knew about the way the world's economy worked.
sentences.zh: “看到我所了解的世界经济运作方式就这样走向终结，这太可怕了。”

sentences.en: The demolished instrumentals leading up to the markets' implosion in the big short are the closest Bertel gets to a vocabulary for what it was like to watch the world crash down.
sentences.zh: 在《大空头》中，市场崩盘前那些被摧毁的器乐演奏，最接近于贝尔特尔为目睹世界崩溃时的感受所找到的词汇。

sentences.en: In 2010, Bertel proposed to Sullivan.
sentences.zh: 2010年，贝尔特尔向沙利文求婚。

sentences.en: A month later, he gave notice.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，他递交了辞呈。

sentences.en: By the time they married, he had started to make trips to Los Angeles, a two-year odyssey of bouncing couches and trying to arrange coffee dates with directors and producers.
sentences.zh: 等他们结婚时，他已经开始前往洛杉矶，开启了一段长达两年的奥德赛之旅——睡遍各处沙发，努力尝试与导演和制片人约咖啡见面。

sentences.en: I was down to do anything, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我当时什么都愿意做。”

sentences.en: I wrote telephone hold music for free.
sentences.zh: “我免费写电话等待音乐。”

sentences.en: For free.
sentences.zh: 免费的。

sentences.en: One evening, Jeremy Kleiner, an executive at
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，B计划娱乐公司（Plan B Entertainment）的高管杰里米·克莱纳（Jeremy Kleiner）出席了一个派对，注意到有人在房间角落里弹奏格什温的曲子。

sentences.en: Plan B Entertainment, attended a party and noticed someone playing Gershwin in the corner of the room.
sentences.zh: 克莱纳说：“我们当时刚刚拿到《为奴十二年》的剧本拍摄许可，实际上还没怎么考虑过作曲是谁。”

sentences.en: We had just gotten a green light for the script of Twelve Years a Slave and hadn't really gotten into the question of composers, Kleiner says.
sentences.zh: “结果就看到这伙计在鸡尾酒会上弹三角钢琴。”

sentences.en: And here's this guy playing on a grand piano at a cocktail party.
sentences.zh: 克莱纳将贝尔特尔介绍给了该片的导演史蒂夫·麦奎因。

sentences.en: Kleiner introduced Bertel to the film's director, Steve McQueen.
sentences.zh: 接着B计划把他介绍给麦凯，然后又介绍给詹金斯，在短短五年内，贝尔特尔就获得了奥斯卡提名。

sentences.en: Then Plan B introduced him to McKay and then to Jenkins, and within five years, Bertel was being nominated for Oscars.
sentences.zh: 如果说贝尔特尔的作品中有一条贯穿始终的线索，那可能就是他对那些做出不和谐走向的缠绵旋律的迷恋。

sentences.en: If there's a through line across Bertel's work, it may be his fascination with winding melodies that make harmonic missteps.
sentences.zh: 最具野心的例子是《副总统》，这是一部带有反英雄色彩的交响乐，其核心跳动着一颗邪恶的心脏。

sentences.en: The most ambitious example is Vice, a kind of anti-heroic symphony with an evil heartbeat at its center.
sentences.zh: 这是一项深厚的技术成就，充斥着双重赋格以及对多种风格流派的暗示，在隐隐指向大乐队爵士乐的同时，又悄然退入独奏

sentences.en: It's a profound technical achievement, buzzing with double fugues and allusions to multiple styles and genres, gesturing toward big band jazz before ducking away into solo
sentences.zh: 钢琴或完整的管弦乐队中。

sentences.en: piano or full orchestra.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也表明了亚当·麦凯对贝尔特尔有多么信任。

sentences.en: But it's also a statement about how much Adam McKay trusts Bertel.
sentences.zh: 麦凯对我说：“我甚至不知道该如何形容我们的工作关系。”

sentences.en: I don't even know how to describe our working relationship, McKay told me.
sentences.zh: “他几乎就像个制作人，因为我一有构思的苗头就会把想法告诉他，然后我和他就会开始不断推敲。”

sentences.en: He's almost like a producer, because I'll tell him the idea from the second I have the premise, and he and I will just start kicking it around.
sentences.zh: 当麦凯开始构思一部嘲讽迪克·切尼的传记片时，贝尔特尔给他发了一条关于马勒第九交响曲的信息。

sentences.en: When McKay was beginning to think about a Dick Cheney mock-you biopic, Bertel sent him a note about Mahler's Ninth.
sentences.zh: 这部交响曲是马勒完成的最后一部交响曲。

sentences.en: The symphony was the last Mahler completed.
sentences.zh: 在创作它的时候，他正饱受心脏病的折磨，生命在慢慢走向终结。

sentences.en: While working on it, he was slowly dying from a heart condition.
sentences.zh: 伦纳德·伯恩斯坦曾指出，该交响曲那畸变、充满打击乐感的开场，正是马勒自身不规律心跳的写照。

sentences.en: Leonard Bernstein suggested that the symphony's skewed, percussive opening was a reflection of Mahler's own uneven heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 对于一部讲述一生屡遭心脏病发作纠缠的人物电影来说，这似乎是一个非常贴切的参考点。

sentences.en: This seemed like an appropriate reference point for a movie about a man whose life has been framed by repeated heart attacks.
sentences.zh: 麦凯开始不断地听《第九交响曲》，并伴随着它来写剧本，当他完成时，

sentences.en: McKay began listening to the Ninth constantly, writing the script to it, and when he finished,
sentences.zh: 贝尔特尔写出了一首扭曲、宏大、带有“第九”风格的配乐。

sentences.en: Bertel wrote a twisted, magisterial, Ninth-like score.
sentences.zh: 《副总统》听起来就像是《彼得与狼》，如果彼得同时也是那只狼的话。

sentences.en: Vice sounds like Peter and the Wolf, if Peter were also the wolf.
sentences.zh: 迪克·切尼的心脏是理解他故事的核心，

sentences.en: Dick Cheney's heart is central to understanding his story,
sentences.zh: 贝尔特尔在工作室里对我说。

sentences.en: Bertel told me in his studio.
sentences.zh: “什么是恶性节律？”

sentences.en: What is a malignant rhythm?
sentences.zh: “从审美的节奏上讲，你该如何对其进行把玩？”

sentences.en: How, rhythmically, could you play with it?
sentences.zh: “然后我也开始在和声上做同样的处理。”

sentences.en: And then I started doing that harmonically as well.
sentences.zh: 他转过身去面对他的Korg Triton键盘——也就是他在“证人保护计划”里用过的那台，缓慢地弹奏着主题，

sentences.en: He turned to his Triton keyboard, the same one he used in the Witness Protection program, and played the theme slowly, landing
sentences.zh: 重重地按在那些不和谐的和弦上，目不转睛地盯着我，仿佛他正在被迪克

sentences.en: hard on the dissonant chords, and staring at me intently, as if he were channeling either Dick
sentences.zh: 切尼或《歌剧魅影》附体一般。

sentences.en: Cheney or the Phantom of the Opera.
sentences.zh: 切尼或歌剧魅影。

sentences.en: It has the shape of something strong, he said, and yet it has a deadly flaw.
sentences.zh: 他说，它有着某种强大事物的轮廓，却又存在着致命的缺陷。

sentences.en: You're reeled in, then repulsed.
sentences.zh: 你被它吸引，随即便感到排斥。

sentences.en: There are intriguing parallels between Bertel and
sentences.zh: 伯特尔与

sentences.en: George Gershwin, another brilliant, energetic Jewish kid who infused the classical canon with the buoyant new genre he loved.
sentences.zh: 乔治·格什温（另一个充满天才与活力的犹太男孩，他将自己热爱的充满生机的全新流派融入了古典音乐正统中）之间存在着耐人寻味的相似之处。

sentences.en: Bertel's most arresting scores tend to fuse both ends of his musical education.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔最引人注目的配乐往往融合了他音乐教育的两端。

sentences.en: Succession is 18th century court music married to heart-pounding beats.
sentences.zh: 《继承之战》是18世纪宫廷音乐与震撼心弦的节拍的结合。

sentences.en: Moonlight chops and screws a classical piano and violin duet as if it's a 3-6 mafia track.
sentences.zh: 《月光男孩》将古典钢琴和小提琴二重奏进行了切碎和放慢处理，听起来就像一首三六帮派（3-6 Mafia）的曲子。

sentences.en: What I've found in the past, John Burlingame told me, is that people have found it impossible to
sentences.zh: 约翰·伯灵格姆（John Burlingame）曾对我说，他过去发现，人们觉得

sentences.en: incorporate such modern musical forms as hip-hop into dramatic underscore for filMs. When Nick did it in moonlight, I was frankly stunned.
sentences.zh: 将嘻哈等现代音乐形式融入电影的戏剧配乐中是不可能的。当尼克在《月光男孩》中做到这一点时，坦白说，我惊呆了。

sentences.en: I didn't think it was possible.
sentences.zh: 我曾认为这是不可能的。

sentences.en: Hip-hop was Bertel's initiation to the fragility of sound, how it could be sampled, stretched, and broken, and somehow, through the breaking, made more powerful.
sentences.zh: 嘻哈是伯特尔对声音脆弱性的启蒙，让他了解到声音如何被采样、拉伸、打破，又不知何故，通过这种打破变得更具力量。

sentences.en: He loves hearing a story in the sounds around notes, the hiss of spun vinyl, or the musician's breathing.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢聆听音符周围声音中的故事，比如黑胶唱片旋转时的嘶嘶声，或者是音乐家的呼吸声。

sentences.en: Bertel's signature may be music that's been through something.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔的标志或许就是那些经历过某种洗礼的音乐。

sentences.en: As Barry Jenkins puts it, a productive line of inquiry for the two of them has been, how can we break this?
sentences.zh: 正如巴里·詹金斯（Barry Jenkins）所说，对他们两人来说，一条富有成效的探究路线一直是：我们该如何打破这一点？

sentences.en: Take the scene in Beale Street, when Daniel struggles to tell Fonny what happened to him in prison, a rape unmistakable in James Baldwin's novel that the movie seems to
sentences.zh: 以《假若街头会说话》中的那一幕为例，丹尼尔极力向方尼诉说他在监狱里的遭遇，这是詹姆斯·鲍德温（James Baldwin）小说中绝无仅有的强暴情节，而电影似乎通过

sentences.en: allude to through Bertel's music and Brian Tyree Henry's remarkable face.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔的音乐和布莱恩·泰瑞·亨利（Brian Tyree Henry）非凡的面部表情暗示了这一点。

sentences.en: On the surface, Miles Davis plays coolly on a record player.
sentences.zh: 表面上，唱片机上播放着迈尔斯·戴维斯（Miles Davis）冷静的爵士乐。

sentences.en: But underneath, Bertel has taken the cellos from Eros, which scored an early romantic scene, and bent them.
sentences.zh: 但在暗地里，伯特尔取用了曾为早期浪漫场景配乐的电影《爱神》中的大提琴声，并将其扭曲。

sentences.en: We talked about it almost like we were harming them, he told me, hurting the sound, making it feel like the sound is damaged.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，我们谈论这件事时，感觉就像是在伤害它们，伤害声音，让声音感觉像是受到了破坏。

sentences.en: You find similar damage in Bertel's breakout score for the big short.
sentences.zh: 你在伯特尔为《大空头》创作的突破性配乐中也能发现类似的破坏感。

sentences.en: As the movie opens in the 1970s, funky horns are the sound of irrational exuberance.
sentences.zh: 当电影在20世纪70年代开场时，放克号角声代表着非理性的繁荣。

sentences.en: Later, when Steve Carell's character realizes the industry is built on 40 years of sand, they return as a faint wine, like a chastened mosquito.
sentences.zh: 后来，当史蒂夫·卡瑞尔（Steve Carell）饰演的角色意识到这个行业是建立在40年的沙丘之上时，它们又作为微弱的哀鸣再次出现，就像一只受挫的蚊子。

sentences.en: That's what happened to his understanding, Bertel said.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔说，这就是他的理解所经历的。

sentences.en: It's been mangled and stretched out and transformed.
sentences.zh: 它被肢解、拉伸并转化了。

sentences.en: The question of what hip-hop means for Bertel may come together most concretely on Succession.
sentences.zh: 嘻哈音乐对伯特尔意味着什么这个问题，在《继承之战》中或许得到了最具体的体现。

sentences.en: He had read the pilot script and visited the set with Adam McKay, who suggested him for the project.
sentences.zh: 他读过试播集剧本，并和亚当·麦凯（Adam McKay）一起去过片场，正是麦凯向剧组推荐了他。

sentences.en: The show had to have gravitas, Jesse Armstrong told him, but it was also deeply absurd, and the music would have to say both these things at once.
sentences.zh: 杰西·阿姆斯特朗（Jesse Armstrong）告诉他，这部剧必须具有威严感，但同时也极其荒诞，音乐必须同时表达这两点。

sentences.en: It wasn't clear how Bertel could make that happen.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚伯特尔将如何实现这一点。

sentences.en: Then he started thinking about Kendall Roy, one of the heirs apparent who anchor the show.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始思考肯德尔·罗伊（Kendall Roy），这位支撑起整部剧的法定继承人之一。

sentences.en: The first thing you see,
sentences.zh: 你看到的第一个画面，

sentences.en: Bertel said, is he's in the back of this car rapping to the Beastie Boys.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔说，是他坐在车后座听着野兽男孩（Beastie Boys）的歌打着拍子。

sentences.en: It's hard not to think about
sentences.zh: 你很难不去把

sentences.en: Kendall as a failed Bertel, a parallel universe version of what he might have been if he had stayed in finance.
sentences.zh: 肯德尔看作一个失败的伯特尔，一个平行宇宙版本的他——如果他留在金融界的话，他可能会成为的那种人。

sentences.en: A Wall Street bro who hides inside his headphones and disconnects from the world he chose.
sentences.zh: 一个藏在耳机里、与自己选择的世界切断联系的华尔街老油条。

sentences.en: The scene, a young man rapping earnestly inside a chauffeured car, offered a window into how the
sentences.zh: 这个场景——一个年轻人在专车里认真地打着说唱节拍——为我们提供了一个窗口，让我们得以窥见

sentences.en: Roy's self-conception might contrast sharply with their destructive incompetence.
sentences.zh: 罗伊一家的自我认知如何与他们破坏性的无能形成鲜明对比。

sentences.en: What if the sound that they imagined for themselves was this dark, courtly, late 1700s harmonic sound?
sentences.zh: 如果他们为自己想象的声音是这种黑暗、宫廷式的、18世纪末的和声呢？

sentences.en: Bertel asked himself.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔自问。

sentences.en: I played Jesse some of these chords, he said, and he was just sort of like, yes.
sentences.zh: 他说，我弹了一些这样的和弦给杰西听，他的反应差不多就是，行啊。

sentences.en: It was just a wonderful, hairs-on-the-back-of-your-neck feeling that you don't often have, Armstrong told me.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特朗告诉我，那是一种美妙的、让人汗毛直立的感觉，这种感觉并不常有。

sentences.en: To get that feeling, to feel like, oh my god, this is something which just feels like the show.
sentences.zh: 为了获得那种感觉，去觉得，哦天哪，这正是那种契合这部剧的感觉。

sentences.en: The waltz-like rhythm reflecting the unsteady dance between the three central siblings was a smart insight that continues to shape the way Armstrong writes the series.
sentences.zh: 这种华尔兹般的节奏反映了三个核心兄弟姐妹之间不稳定的舞蹈，这是一个绝妙的洞察，它至今仍在塑造阿姆斯特朗创作该剧的方式。

sentences.en: The show's addictive title sequence was the last recording Bertel made for season one.
sentences.zh: 这部剧令人欲罢不能的片头曲是伯特尔为第一季录制的最后一段音乐。

sentences.en: He had structured the season's music like a symphony.
sentences.zh: 他把这一季的音乐结构得像一部交响乐。

sentences.en: The title theme, like an overture, introduces you to all the elements you'll hear in the show, which Bertel recited for me.
sentences.zh: 片头主题曲就像一首序曲，向你介绍了你在剧中将听到所有元素，伯特尔为我细数了这些元素。

sentences.en: The beguiling melody, the detuned pianos, the cello melody, the idea of these huge beats, the weird sleigh bell.
sentences.zh: 迷人的旋律、走音的钢琴、大提琴旋律、宏大节拍的概念、诡异的雪橇铃。

sentences.en: The sleigh bell?
sentences.zh: 雪橇铃？

sentences.en: That's its own thing,
sentences.zh: 那是它独特的东西，

sentences.en: Bertel admitted.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔承认。

sentences.en: That actually doesn't appear in other parts of the show.
sentences.zh: 那实际上并没有出现在剧集的其他部分中。

sentences.en: The main theme is everything but brighter.
sentences.zh: 主旋律包罗万象，只是更加明快。

sentences.en: You're presented with these ideas, so you will both recognize them, but also notice how they change, and you'll have this set of expectations.
sentences.zh: 你接触到这些理念，这样你既能认出它们，又能注意到它们是如何变化的，并且你会有这样一套心理预期。

sentences.en: This is the world you're about to enter.
sentences.zh: 这就是你即将进入的世界。

sentences.en: When Bertel sent the title theme to the production team, he reminded himself that the nature of his profession is adapting.
sentences.zh: 当伯特尔将片头主题曲发送给制作团队时，他提醒自己，他这个职业的本质就是适应。

sentences.en: He's used to coming up with a hundred ideas, presenting a director a few dozen, and possibly seeing them all rejected.
sentences.zh: 他习惯了想出一百个点子，向导演呈现几十个，然后可能看着它们全部被拒绝。

sentences.en: But he also thought, I really don't know what to do if they don't like this.
sentences.zh: 但他也想过，如果他们不喜欢这个，我真的不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: I'll never forget it, Bertel said.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔说，我永远不会忘记那一刻。

sentences.en: Jesse sent an email back, and he was like, I think the right words for this are f*** yeah.
sentences.zh: 杰西回了一封邮件，他的意思是，我觉得形容这个最合适的词就是“他妈的太棒了”。

sentences.en: As Jenkins and I sat on the little studio couch, Bertel played an early sketch for the opening of the Underground Railroad.
sentences.zh: 当詹金斯和我坐在小工作室的沙发上时，伯特尔播放了《地下铁道》开场的一个早期草稿。

sentences.en: A violin bent into a brass fanfare, and then a piano waltzed in, suggesting mystery.
sentences.zh: 一把小提琴被扭曲成铜管乐器的号角声，随后一架钢琴跳着华尔兹登场，暗示着神秘感。

sentences.en: Another winding melody that makes bewitching missteps.
sentences.zh: 另一段蜿蜒曲折的旋律，带来了迷人而美妙的失误。

sentences.en: At this point, he and Jenkins had about three hours of music drafted, and at least as many still to go.
sentences.zh: 此时，他和詹金斯已经起草了大约三个小时的音乐，还有至少同样多的音乐等待完成。

sentences.en: He scrolled down a long list of file names.
sentences.zh: 他在一个长长的文件名列表向下滚动。

sentences.en: Some of these things, we have a sort of very loose, amorphous idea, he said, hitting play on another piece.
sentences.zh: 其中一些东西，我们只有一个非常宽泛、模糊的想法，他说着，按下了另一段音乐的播放键。

sentences.en: So this is an idea of descending downward.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个向下延伸的概念。

sentences.en: I think this comes from the cicada, Jenkins said, just that one melody.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯说，我觉得这来自蝉鸣，就那一段旋律。

sentences.en: He started singing softly.
sentences.zh: 他轻声哼唱起来。

sentences.en: Jenkins had been making recordings on set, collecting natural sounds that
sentences.zh: 詹金斯一直在片场进行录音，收集自然之声，而

sentences.en: Bertel would pitch down to make instruments.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔会把这些声音的音高调低来制作乐器。

sentences.en: The piano track he'd played me earlier started out as a field recording, the whistle of cicadas and bird noise, an airy crackling that turned out to be cotton.
sentences.zh: 他之前播放给我的钢琴曲最初是一段实地录音，里面有蝉鸣声和鸟叫声，还有一种听起来像棉花的轻柔爆裂声。

sentences.en: I just do play-doh with some of this audio, Bertel said, filtering out high frequencies and adding reverb until the cicadas sounded blurry and spectral.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔说，我对其中一些音频只是用类似玩泥巴的方式进行处理，过滤掉高频并添加混响，直到蝉鸣声听起来模糊而如梦似幻。

sentences.en: In one track, an insect caught in the play-doh turned into a bell, tolling the same three ghostly notes.
sentences.zh: 在一首曲子里，一只被困在“泥巴”里的昆虫变成了一个钟，敲响了同样三个幽灵般的音符。

sentences.en: We don't know what that is, by the way, Jenkins said.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们不知道那是什么，

sentences.en: We just call him Fred now.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯说，我们现在只管叫他弗雷德。

sentences.en: Bertel started a new piano track, Jenkins, and this piano was to match, Bertel, trying to match Fred's melody, Jenkins.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔启动了一个新的钢琴轨道，詹金斯，而这台钢琴是为了配合，伯特尔，试图配合弗雷德的旋律，詹金斯。

sentences.en: So Fred the Bug has to get a co-producer credit.
sentences.zh: 所以小虫弗雷德必须获得一个联合制作人的署名。

sentences.en: Jenkins had also been drawn to the noises of the human environment during the shoot.
sentences.zh: 在拍摄期间，詹金斯也被人类环境的噪声所吸引。

sentences.en: We were shooting down in Savannah, he said, and there was a construction site next to our set, and I was
sentences.zh: 他说，我们在萨凡纳（Savannah）拍摄，我们的片场旁边有一个建筑工地，当时我就

sentences.en: like, oh, that drill has a really nice rhythm to it, and so I had the PAs go out and record it and sent it to Nick.
sentences.zh: 觉得，哦，那个钻机的节奏感真的很好，所以我让制片助理（PA）出去把它录下来并发送给了尼克。

sentences.en: Bertel started laughing.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔笑了起来。

sentences.en: I remember getting these texts from you in the middle of the day, he said, and it was just noise.
sentences.zh: 他说，我记得在白天收到过你发来的这些短信，里面全都是噪音。

sentences.en: There's a slight Willy Wonka vibe to Bertel in his studio, and as I processed Fred and the drill, he and Jenkins grinned like the inventors of the everlasting gobstopper.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔和他的工作室带有一种轻微的威利·旺卡（Willy Wonka）式的气质，当我理清了弗雷德和钻机的事后，他和詹金斯笑得就像是“永恒不灭大口嚼糖果”的发明者一样。

sentences.en: Over time, the two have grown more comfortable with thinking about a score in terms of manipulated recordings, not just a composition for instruments.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，这两人在通过处理过的录音——而不仅仅是为乐器谱曲——来构思配乐方面变得越来越游刃有余。

sentences.en: If everything's in context, Bertel said, the drill is music.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔说，如果一切都在情理之中，钻孔机就是音乐。

sentences.en: In Moonlight, they used ocean sounds.
sentences.zh: 在《月光男孩》中，他们使用了海洋的声音。

sentences.en: In Beale Street, subways.
sentences.zh: 在《假若街头会说话》中，他们使用了地铁的声音。

sentences.en: They were looking forward to getting new fire sounds.
sentences.zh: 他们非常期待能收集到新的火的声音。

sentences.en: We actually do have people on set burning things, Jenkins said.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯说，我们实际上在片场安排了人来焚烧东西。

sentences.en: Bertel queued up early footage from the show.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔调出了该剧早期的素材片段。

sentences.en: Images of an enslaved family in ragged clothing, faces stinging with confrontation.
sentences.zh: 画面中是一个衣衫褴褛的被奴役家庭，他们的脸上写满了抗争的刺痛。

sentences.en: A white-haired black man standing alone in a cotton field as cicada noises crackled, as if the field were catching fire.
sentences.zh: 一个白发苍苍的黑人男子独自站在棉花地里，蝉鸣声沙沙作响，仿佛棉花地正燃起大火。

sentences.en: Two young black women seated at a dance, a man bowing and offering his hand.
sentences.zh: 两个年轻的黑人女性坐在舞会上，一个男人鞠躬并伸出了手。

sentences.en: A fairytale sequence that feels more like a horror movie.
sentences.zh: 这是一段比起童话更像是恐怖电影的序列。

sentences.en: I don't mind the fire being out by that point, Jenkins said, right as he reached for her hand.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯说，就在他伸手去拉她的那一刻，我并不介意大火在那时已经熄灭。

sentences.en: Didn't fully understand what they were up to, until Bertel played me a trailer they made for the
sentences.zh: 直到伯特尔为我播放了他们为

sentences.en: Television Critics Association, a summary of the show's music that starts with frantic arpeggios,
sentences.zh: 电视评论家协会（Television Critics Association）制作的预告片之前，我并没有完全理解他们在搞什么名堂。那是一段该剧音乐的总结，以疯狂的琶音开场，

sentences.en: almost unbearably high, then moves through the waltzing mid-range of the Fred the Bug piano melody
sentences.zh: 高亢得几乎令人难以忍受，接着过渡到弗雷德小虫钢琴旋律的华尔兹中音区，

sentences.en: and settles gradually into a resonant bass.
sentences.zh: 并逐渐沉落到一个共鸣低音中。

sentences.en: It's that descending idea, he said, going underground, going downward.
sentences.zh: 他说，这就是那个下沉的概念，深入地下，向下延伸。

sentences.en: The final bass notes were made from the sounds of the drill.
sentences.zh: 最后的低音是由钻孔机的声音制作出来的。

sentences.en: You literally hit earth.
sentences.zh: 你真的触及到了大地。

sentences.en: They weren't drawn to the drill just because they wanted to allude to the show's title.
sentences.zh: 他们被钻孔机吸引，并不仅仅是因为他们想暗示该剧的标题。

sentences.en: It was an attraction Jenkins had to a sound that felt right and then became right.
sentences.zh: 这是詹金斯对一种听起来对劲、随后又变得真正对劲的声音产生的吸引力。

sentences.en: We start with an idea, Bertel said.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔说，我们从一个想法开始。

sentences.en: It's a feeling.
sentences.zh: 那是一种感觉。

sentences.en: It could even be really subtle.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可以非常微妙。

sentences.en: That's why I'm so sensitive to these early things.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我对这些早期的东西如此敏感。

sentences.en: We need those early places.
sentences.zh: 我们需要这些最初的切入点。

sentences.en: And the great part is when you start with these things and you don't know why, and then they actually start to make sense,
sentences.zh: 而最棒的部分是，当你从这些东西开始却又不知其所以然时，它们实际上开始变得有意义了，

sentences.en: Jenkins said.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯说。

sentences.en: And you're just like, oh, that's why we've been following this.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会觉得，哦，原来这就是我们一直在追寻的方向。

sentences.en: Sitting in the dark with empty bottles of seltzer, none of us could have anticipated that the world was about to shut down.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在黑暗中，面对着空荡荡的苏打水瓶，谁也没有料到这个世界即将按下面暂停键。

sentences.en: By the time the show neared completion a year later, Bertel and Jenkins would be engaged in their most radical experiments to date.
sentences.zh: 一年后，当该剧接近尾声时，伯特尔和詹金斯将投入到他们迄今为止最激进的实验中。

sentences.en: By that point, Bertel's language for parts of the project were bracingly tactile.
sentences.zh: 到那个时候，伯特尔对该项目部分内容的描述带有令人振奋的触感。

sentences.en: He spoke of stripping sounds down to an abrasive, raw surface, peeling them to their bones.
sentences.zh: 他谈到将声音剥离到一种具有摩擦力的、原始的表面，将其剥离至骨髓。

sentences.en: When he bent notes enough, he says, they revealed whole other characters.
sentences.zh: 他说，当他把音符弯曲到一定程度时，它们就会展现出完全不同的角色。

sentences.en: The Underground Railroad emerged from last year broken and changed, but still recognizable.
sentences.zh: 《地下铁道》从去年的境况中走出，虽然饱受摧残、面目全非，但依然清晰可辨。

sentences.en: You can feel that February session still underfoot.
sentences.zh: 你依然能感受到那场二月会议留下的足迹。

sentences.en: It all winds up somewhere, Bertel had told me.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔曾对我说，这一切最终都会归于某个地方。

sentences.en: There's no wrong turn.
sentences.zh: 没有错误的转弯。

sentences.en: As we wrapped up, Jenkins concluded, the piano just works for the show.
sentences.zh: 当我们结束时，詹金斯总结道，这架钢琴对这部剧来说简直绝配。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Like, I can see the episodes when I hear this stuff.
sentences.zh: 就像是，当我听到这些音乐时，我眼前就能浮现出剧中的那些单集。

sentences.en: And what's so interesting is at no point in any of the other projects did we feel that way,
sentences.zh: 而最有趣的是，在其他任何项目的任何阶段，我们都没有过这种感觉，

sentences.en: Bertel said.
sentences.zh: 伯特尔说。

sentences.en: The piano's just the bedrock, man, Jenkins said.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯说，钢琴就是基石，老兄。

sentences.en: The piano and Fred.
sentences.zh: 钢琴和弗雷德。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党便陷入了一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的权力争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我莎拉·凯尼格（Sarah Koenig）主持的最新一期播客《都市》（Metro）中，我们将讲述人们试图维持其影响力却又在过程中失控的故事。

sentences.zh: 《都市》。yyds
